verdict: Camden's property revenue fell 4% to $381M after it sold its California portfolio, but that sale produced a $974M gain that lifted net income attributable to shareholders to $900M.

kpis.label: Property revenue
kpis.note: -4% vs a year ago — rent and other property income. The chart's top line is $1,355M of total money in, including the one-off sale gain below.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.00 a year ago — includes about $9.37 a share of gain on the California sale, less $0.83 a share of impairments

kpis.label: FFO per share (diluted)
kpis.note: Funds From Operations — the REIT-standard profit measure, which adds back property depreciation and removes sale gains; Core FFO was $1.71

kpis.label: Gain on sale of properties
kpis.note: Selling 11 California communities (3,620 apartment homes) for about $1.6B

segments.name: Rental revenues
segments.note: Rent from apartment leases. Camden gives an approximate split of its $381M of property revenue: about $338M was rent, down from about $352M a year ago as the sold California homes left the portfolio.

segments.name: Other property income
segments.note: Amounts in lease contracts for services other than rent itself — about $43M of property revenue, down from about $44M a year ago (approximate split given by Camden).

segments.name: Gain on sale of properties
segments.note: Selling the whole California portfolio — 11 communities, 3,620 apartment homes — for about $1.6B on July 29, 2026 booked this one-off gain. It is not rent and will not repeat; about $0.9B of the proceeds repaid borrowing.

opex.name: Property management and G&A
opex.note: Property management $9M, fee and asset management expenses $1M, and general and administrative $18M — Camden's smaller running-cost lines, grouped together so the chart stays readable.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the apartment buildings over their useful lives. This is a paper cost — no cash leaves — which is why REITs add it back in Funds From Operations.

opex.name: Land impairment
opex.note: Impairment of land development assets — writing down land held for development to what Camden now thinks it is worth. Treated as a one-off — see one-time items.

otherDetail: Other items were -$32M, net: $41M of interest expense, partly offset by $8M of fee and interest income from non-property activities and a $1M benefit in other non-operating items. Two deferred-compensation lines (about $2M each) cancel each other out and are left out of the flow. The $974M sale gain is counted as money in at the left of the chart, not here.

takeaways.title: A big property sale dominates the quarter
takeaways.text: On July 29 Camden sold its whole California portfolio — 11 communities, 3,620 homes — for about $1.6B and booked a $974M gain. About $0.9B of the money repaid borrowing. The gain is why EPS jumped to $8.71 from $1.00 a year ago.

takeaways.title: The apartments themselves were steady
takeaways.text: For homes Camden owned in both periods, revenue was almost flat (-0.1% YoY) and occupancy was 95.6%. Renewing tenants paid 3.6% more, while new leases signed for 2.0% less. Total revenue fell mainly because the sold California homes are gone, not because the remaining homes weakened.

takeaways.title: The REIT measure barely moved
takeaways.text: Funds From Operations was $1.70 a share, up from $1.67 a year ago, and Core FFO was $1.71, almost flat. FFO strips out the sale gain and the $86M land write-down and adds back depreciation, so it shows a steadier business than the $900M headline profit suggests. Camden also bought three communities for $305M in the quarter.

oneTimers: Gain on sale of properties: $974M from selling the California portfolio (11 communities, 3,620 homes) for about $1.6B on July 29, 2026. Without this gain, Camden would have reported a loss this quarter — it is a one-off, not rent.
Impairment: Camden wrote down land development assets by $86M (recording that the land is worth less than its book value). Camden treats this as non-core and excludes it from Core FFO.
footerNote: Adapted: the $974M California sale gain is counted as money in alongside rent (total $1,355M; property revenue alone $381M).
follow100Note: An unusual quarter: this $100 is $100 of everything that came in — about $25 of rent, $3 of other property income and $72 from selling the California portfolio. Camden's property revenue on its own was $381M.
